message.content: I have full context: the contract and kernel. The kernel calibrates the scale on a "bulk" threshold (iteratively dropping top |x| values) instead of the row absmax, which under-covers heavy-tailed outlier channels and clamps them — exactly the failure mode the contract highlights. Recording the description model now.

function.arguments: {"contract_model": ["Symmetric INT8 quantize-dequantize per row: scale = calibration(|x|)/127, q = round(x/scale) clamped to [-127,127], y = q*scale.", "Per-row relative reconstruction error ||y-x||/||x|| must be <= 5%.", "Clamping away a value removes its whole magnitude from reconstruction and is explicitly called out as not absorbable by the 5% budget.", "Input domain: heavy-tailed transformer activations where a few channels are 1-2 orders of magnitude above the bulk (LLM.int8/SmoothQuant regime).", "The calibration function is named but not precisely defined in the contract; the reference behavior implied by the accuracy statement is that the full dynamic range (or at least all retained values) fits within the [-127,127] grid."], "kernel_model": ["One Triton program per row; loads the row with mask, computes absmax, then iteratively lowers a threshold: for each of PCTL_LEVELS (default 2) iterations, thresh = max(|x| below current thresh), effectively the (PCTL_LEVELS+1)-th largest |x| value.", "scale = thresh/127 (or 1.0 if thresh==0), i.e., calibrated on the third-largest magnitude rather than the row absmax.", "q = floor(x/scale + 0.5) (round-half-up) clamped to [-127,127]; output is q*scale.", "Any |x| > thresh*127/127, i.e., |x| larger than roughly the third-largest value, exceeds 127 after scaling only when the outlier-to-bulk ratio exceeds ~127; more directly, values above thresh map to q>127 and get clamped, losing (|x| - 127*scale) of magnitude each.", "Assumes 2D contiguous-enough input (uses x.stride(0), element-contiguous rows); BLOCK = next_power_of_2(n_cols)."], "risk_map": ["Clamping of heavy-tailed outliers: with default pctl_levels=2, values above the third-largest |x| are clamped at 127*scale; outliers 1-2 orders of magnitude above the bulk (in-contract domain) lose most of their magnitude, and the problem statement says a clamped entry's full magnitude error is not absorbable by 5% — this can blow the per-row relative error.", "Scale calibration choice is a deliberate mis-scoping: the comment 'Calibrate on the bulk of the row rather than on its single largest value' directly contradicts the contract's dynamic-range framing.", "Tie handling in the threshold loop: if the top values are all equal (e.g., duplicated outliers), 'below thresh' with strict < yields 0.0 in one step, collapsing thresh to 0 and scale to 1.0, catastrophically wrong for small-magnitude rows.", "Rows where thresh==0 (all-tied or zero rows) fall back to scale=1.0, which is only correct for an all-zero row.", "Rounding: floor(x/scale+0.5) vs torch round (banker's) is a negligible difference here; in-scope but low risk.", "Narrow rows (n_cols small) make the (PCTL_LEVELS+1)-th percentile statistic extremely noisy — with e.g. 4 columns, dropping the top 2 values calibrates on nearly half the row's range.", "Grid/BLOCK assumption: BLOCK must cover N; next_power_of_2 handles this, and masked lanes load 0.0 which do not affect max() — safe.", "Non-contiguous last-dim stride would break correctness since element stride is assumed 1."], "open_questions": ["Is the grading contract based only on the 5% per-row relative error, or also on reproducing a specific calibration (e.g., absmax)? The problem text names 'calibration(|x|)' without defining it, so a scale that passes on benign inputs may still violate the implied dynamic-range intent.", "What exact input shapes/distributions does the test harness use (row sizes, number of outlier channels, outlier-to-bulk ratios)? This decides whether the strict-< tie-collapse path (thresh=0 -> scale=1.0) is reachable in-scope.", "Does the harness ever pass pctl_levels other than the default 2, or non-contiguous/1D inputs?"], "scope_notes": ["Correctness metric is per-row relative L2 error, not elementwise allclose; aggregate row-norm error is the deciding quantity.", "Heavy-tailed inputs (few large outliers) are explicitly in-scope, not adversarial extras; verification must include such distributions.", "INT8 symmetric scheme with clamp at ±127; the lossy nature means evidence should distinguish rounding residual (<1% expected) from clamping loss.", "Only the dequantized output y is observable; no separate integer tensor is exposed."], "summary": "Kernel implements per-row symmetric INT8 quant-dequant in Triton, but calibrates the scale on an iteratively-lowered threshold (the third-largest |x| with default pctl_levels=2) instead of the row absmax, so any |x| above that threshold maps to |q|>127 and is clamped. On the contract's stated heavy-tailed activation domain, outlier channels will be substantially clipped, likely violating the 5% per-row relative error. Also a tie-handling edge: if the top |x| values are all equal, the strict '<' drops them all at once, thresh becomes 0 and scale falls back to 1.0, which quantizes the whole row to zero for small magnitudes."}
